name: Extensile lateral approach to the calcaneus
corridor: Full-thickness lateral calcaneal artery flap elevated strictly subperiosteally with the lateral ligaments and inferior peroneal retinaculum

positioning.text: Position lateral or floppy lateral with the operative hindfoot uppermost and supported so the lateral calcaneus and fluoroscopic views remain accessible.

setup.text: Delay surgery until swelling has subsided and lateral skin wrinkles return; protect fracture blisters and confirm flap viability before incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the Achilles tendon, lateral malleolus, base of the fifth metatarsal, junction of lateral and plantar skin, and posterior midline.

incision.text: Create a gently curved L-shaped incision with the vertical limb posterior to the lateral malleolus/Achilles border and the horizontal limb at the lateral–plantar skin junction toward the fifth-metatarsal base.

superficial_interval.text: Cut directly to bone at the corner and raise one full-thickness flap without undermining skin or separating the lateral calcaneal arterial supply.

deep_interval.text: Continue strictly subperiosteally, elevating periosteum, lateral collateral ligament, and inferior peroneal retinaculum together; split abductor digiti minimi in line with its fibers.

layers.text: Skin and full-thickness soft-tissue flap, subperiosteal lateral-wall plane with ligament/retinacular sleeve, lateral calcaneal wall, then subtalar posterior facet.

structures_encountered.text: The flap contains the lateral calcaneal arterial network, sural nerve, peroneal tendons and retinaculum, lateral ankle ligaments, abductor digiti minimi, and periosteum.

structures_at_risk.text: The lateral calcaneal artery and its anastomoses are the critical flap blood supply; leaving the subperiosteal plane or malpositioning either incision limb risks necrosis.
The sural nerve is at risk near the superior vertical limb and should be protected by correct posterior incision placement rather than aggressive isolation.

danger_zones.text: Do not place the vertical limb too anterior, the horizontal limb too superior, or dissect off the periosteum; each error jeopardizes flap perfusion and wound healing.

retraction_hazards.text: Use gentle periosteal sutures or carefully placed retractors; avoid fibular K-wire retraction that can injure the lateral calcaneal artery and increase wound breakdown.

exposure.text: Provides broad visualization of the lateral calcaneal wall, tuberosity, anterior process, calcaneocuboid region, and posterior subtalar facet.

limitations.text: The approach is invasive and soft-tissue dependent; it carries more wound risk than limited approaches and should not be used through swollen or compromised skin.

extensions.text: The distal subperiosteal interval can be developed toward the calcaneocuboid joint, while posterior-facet visualization can be increased between flexor hallucis longus and peroneal tendons.

indications.text: Used for ORIF of displaced intra-articular and severe calcaneal fractures and selected elective hindfoot reconstructions requiring broad lateral visualization.

relative_contraindications.text: Do not proceed with substantial swelling, absent wrinkle sign, threatened lateral skin, active infection, or patient factors that make flap healing unacceptably unreliable.

implant_implications.text: Keep plates and prominent hardware away from the flap apex and verify that fixation does not entrap peroneal tendons or penetrate the subtalar joint.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Maintain access for lateral, axial heel, and Broden-type subtalar views to assess reduction, height, width, alignment, and joint penetration.

closure.text: Perform tension-free layered closure of deep fascia and abductor fascia followed by meticulous skin closure; use a drain selectively to limit hematoma.

complications.text: Key complications are flap-tip necrosis, wound dehiscence, deep infection, sural neuropathy, peroneal-tendon irritation, subtalar stiffness, and hardware prominence.

bailouts.text: If the flap appears ischemic or cannot close without tension, stop further insult, reassess fixation prominence, obtain soft-tissue expertise, and use staged or alternative management rather than forced closure.

procedure_applications.condition: Broad visualization of a displaced intra-articular or severe calcaneal fracture is required
Extensile lateral hindfoot access is selected

questions.question: What clinical sign is commonly used to judge readiness for extensile lateral calcaneal surgery?
questions.answer: Return of lateral skin wrinkles—the wrinkle sign.

questions.question: Which artery is central to survival of the lateral calcaneal flap?
questions.answer: The lateral calcaneal artery, usually a terminal branch of the peroneal artery.

questions.question: What deep-dissection plane protects the flap blood supply?
questions.answer: A strictly subperiosteal plane with periosteum and retinacular/ligamentous tissue elevated as one flap.
